nrsf_cc.label: Climate-controlled net rentable sq ft
nrsf_cc.assumption: A hypothetical climate-controlled building of about 30,000 net rentable square feet, sized as the larger half of a two-product facility because the census found climate control on the operators' own sites only at Heartland and Bluegrass among the Bardstown operators it confirmed [^19,20].

nrsf_du.label: Drive-up net rentable sq ft
nrsf_du.assumption: About 24,000 square feet of drive-up units. Every other confirmed operator sells drive-up space [^21,22,23], so a drive-up wing keeps the entry price point that local tenants already know.

land_acres.label: Site area, acres
land_acres.assumption: A hypothetical site of about 3 acres on the US 150 corridor. It holds two single-story buildings, drive aisles, a gate and the open space and setbacks of the B-3 district [^8]; no particular tract is assumed.

land_per_acre.label: Land price per acre
land_per_acre.assumption: The research holds no closed land sale in Bardstown, only asking prices for listed tracts, which this study does not use. $160,000 per acre is a round placeholder for improved commercial land in town; the appraisal replaces it.

cost_cc.label: Climate-controlled building cost per net rentable sq ft
cost_cc.assumption: The research found no Bardstown construction cost index or bid. $62 is a placeholder for an insulated single-story metal building with heating, cooling and dehumidification, and the contractor's bid must replace it.

cost_du.label: Drive-up building cost per net rentable sq ft
cost_du.assumption: A placeholder for uninsulated drive-up buildings with roll-up doors, about half the climate-controlled cost per foot; a bid replaces it.

site_work.label: Site work, paving, drainage, fencing and gate
site_work.assumption: A lump sum for grading, stormwater, paved aisles, fencing, lighting and a keypad gate. Bardstown requires a land disturbance permit and stormwater review for a site of this kind [^11]; the civil engineer's estimate replaces the allowance.

contingency_pct.label: Hard-cost contingency
contingency_pct.assumption: 7% of hard cost, because bids and subsurface conditions are not yet known.

soft_pct.label: Soft costs, share of hard cost
soft_pct.assumption: Engineering, site plan review, permits, legal, appraisal, the feasibility study and construction-period interest.

fixtures.label: Office, security, access control and software
fixtures.assumption: A working allowance for the rental office, cameras, gate and door alarm hardware and management software; no benchmark found.

working_capital.label: Lease-up reserve and pre-opening costs
working_capital.assumption: Covers marketing, payroll and utilities while the units fill. Nothing in the research measures how fast a new Bardstown facility leases up, so the reserve is sized to the Year 1 shortfall the model shows.

cc_rate.label: Climate-controlled rent per sq ft per month
cc_rate.assumption: No Bardstown operator posts a climate-controlled rate: the confirmed operators' own sites list none [^19,20,22,23], and the research could not date the aggregator rates it found, so this page does not print them. $1.00 a square foot (a 10 by 10 unit at $100 a month) is a placeholder set above the drive-up rate, with 3% annual growth as an allowance; a secret-shopper survey replaces it.

cc_occ.label: Climate-controlled occupancy, share of net rentable area
cc_occ.assumption: A ramp to a stabilized level in Year 3. The research holds no occupancy for any Bardstown competitor, so the ramp is a placeholder that the competitor survey must test.

du_rate.label: Drive-up rent per sq ft per month
du_rate.assumption: No operator in the census posts a verified drive-up rate on its own site [^21,22,23]. $0.60 a square foot (a 10 by 10 at $60 a month) is a placeholder below the climate rate; the survey replaces it.

du_occ.label: Drive-up occupancy, share of net rentable area
du_occ.assumption: Faster than the climate wing because the product is the one the market already buys, and held below full because the census shows many drive-up competitors [^21,22,23].

other_pct.label: Fees, tenant insurance and retail, share of rent
other_pct.assumption: Administrative fees, tenant protection plans, lock and box sales; no local benchmark.

payroll.label: Payroll and benefits (Year 1)
payroll.assumption: One resident or full-time manager and part-time cover. Climate-controlled competitors advertise on-site or remote management [^19,20]; the owner's staffing plan replaces this allowance.

utilities_pct.label: Utilities, share of revenue
utilities_pct.assumption: Heating, cooling and dehumidification for the climate wing, plus lighting and gate power; the engineer's load estimate replaces it.

rm_pct.label: Repairs and maintenance, share of revenue
rm_pct.assumption: Roofs, doors, paving, HVAC service and the gate.

marketing_pct.label: Marketing and booking fees, share of revenue
marketing_pct.assumption: Search and aggregator listings, signage and online rental software fees.

ga_pct.label: Administration and professional fees, share of revenue

mgmt_pct.label: Management fee, share of revenue
mgmt_pct.assumption: The research found no management fee norm for independent facilities. 3% is carried so the projection pays for oversight even if the owner runs the site.

insurance.label: Insurance (Year 1)
insurance.assumption: Insurance terms were NOT FOUND. $19,000 is a placeholder for a metal-building facility; the lender needs a bound quote that includes wind and tornado cover.

tax_city.label: City of Bardstown tax rate, FY 2025-26 ($0.1610 per $100)

tax_city_schools.label: Bardstown City Schools real property rate ($0.7910 per $100)

tax_county.label: Nelson County Fiscal Court rate, 2024 ($0.1200 per $100)

tax_other.label: State and library rates
tax_other.assumption: Dated rates for the state and the library district were NOT FOUND; a broker site printed components from mixed years, which this study does not use. About 0.16% is carried until the Kentucky Department of Revenue rate book is read.

growth_tax.label: Taxable value growth per year
growth_tax.assumption: An allowance for reassessment by the Nelson County property valuation administrator; the study makes no forecast of assessed values.

growth_payroll.label: Payroll growth per year
growth_payroll.assumption: An allowance for wage growth; no local wage series for storage staff was found.

growth_insurance.label: Insurance growth per year
growth_insurance.assumption: An allowance for premium increases on a metal-building facility in a tornado-prone region; a bound quote replaces it.

reserve_psf.label: Replacement reserve per net rentable sq ft per year
reserve_psf.assumption: A small allowance for roofs, doors and HVAC replacement; no benchmark found.

growth_reserve.label: Reserve growth per year
growth_reserve.assumption: Labelled allowance for replacement cost inflation.

usda_fee_paydown.label: Retention fee base decline per year
usda_fee_paydown.assumption: The model applies the retention fee to the outstanding guaranteed balance (the terms sheet prints no base) and lowers that base by 3% of the original balance each year, a labelled simplification.

bi_fee_pct.label: USDA guarantee fee: 3.0% initial plus 0.50% for a guarantee issued before construction is complete (the model applies it to the guaranteed amount; the terms sheet prints no base)

bi_annual_fee.label: USDA annual retention fee (the model applies it to the outstanding guaranteed balance; the terms sheet prints no base)

bi_rate.label: Interest rate
bi_rate.assumption: B&I rates are negotiated between lender and borrower [^26]. Prime was 7.00% on October 9, 2026 [^35]; this study carries Prime plus 0.75 points and the lender sets the rate at pricing.

bi_amort_years.label: Amortization
bi_amort_years.assumption: USDA allows a term up to the useful life of the project or collateral, with a maximum of 40 years or the state-statute limit, whichever is less [^26]. Metal buildings, roofs, paving and HVAC wear out sooner, so the model amortizes over 25 years.

bi_equity_min_pct.label: Minimum equity
bi_equity_min_pct.assumption: The USDA terms sheet prints no equity minimum for B&I. The study tests 25% of project cost, a lender-style figure; the lender must confirm the requirement in its credit memo.

bi_dscr_floor.label: Coverage floor
bi_dscr_floor.assumption: The USDA terms sheet prints no coverage ratio for B&I; the lender's credit policy governs. The study tests 1.25x in Year 3, the first stabilized year.

uses.label: Site work, paving, drainage, fencing and gate
Soft costs, permits and construction interest

revenue.label: Climate-controlled rent
revenue.basis: sq ft x occupancy x 12 x rate

revenue.label: Drive-up rent
revenue.basis: sq ft x occupancy x 12 x rate

opex.label: Property tax
opex.expr: (land_acres * land_per_acre + (nrsf_cc * cost_cc + nrsf_du * cost_du + site_work) * (1 + contingency_pct)) * (tax_city + tax_city_schools + tax_county + tax_other) * (1 + growth_tax) ** y

opex.label: USDA annual retention fee (passed through)
opex.expr: tpc * (1 - bi_equity_min_pct) * bi_guarantee_pct * bi_annual_fee * (1 - usda_fee_paydown * y)

proposed.note: the sponsor proposes a USDA-guaranteed loan for the balance
